title: Session orchestration shim: map OpenAI Chat Completions requests/responses to Redwood runtime
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Implement a session-level compatibility shim that translates incoming OpenAI Chat Completions (messages/temperature/top_p/stop/etc.) into Redwood internal request shape and converts Redwood streaming and final responses back to OpenAI-compatible payloads. The shim must preserve observable semantics for legacy clients (message ordering, incremental deltas, function/tool call framing) while leveraging Redwood features (prefix KV caching, batching, model variant fallbacks). Key goals: preserve function-call fidelity, stable SSE/event ordering, idempotent message IDs, and minimal latency impact for streaming flows.
acceptance_criteria: Requests with messages+functions are accepted and execute with the same function selection behavior as OpenAI when configured in compatibility mode
Streaming responses follow OpenAI delta sequencing: incremental 'content' tokens emitted with identical SSE framing and final 'finish_reason' mapping
Tool/function calls from models are emitted as OpenAI-style function_call events when client expects them, including name, arguments (stringified JSON), and final invocation lifecycle events
Session affinity and idempotency: replaying the same request (same client-provided idempotency_key) should not re-execute expensive side-effects if flagged
Schema-preserving structured outputs: Redwood structured output objects are serialized into the legacy content/choices shape and include a deterministic mapping table in telemetry
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: streaming re-ordering due to internal batching could break client expectations. Mitigation: implement a thin per-session sequence window that orders chunks before SSE emission and adds a small configurable reordering buffer (default 10ms)
Risk: function call argument shapes differ between model and Redwood tool API. Mitigation: add an argument normalizer that enforces stringified JSON and retains original offsets for diagnostics

Risk: preserving legacy OpenAI fields (e.g., 'usage' tokens) imposes cost. Mitigation: generate best-effort usage estimates and mark as 'estimated' in response; surface precise billing in payment/usage dashboards instead
implementation_notes: Behavior mode: default to 'compat-strict' for signed legacy projects; runtime flag allows 'compat-lax' to drop non-essential edges for performance
Map OpenAI 'messages' array: preserve role mapping (user/system/assistant) but collapse consecutive system messages into a single system prefix to match Redwood's prompt-prefix optimization
Handle OpenAI 'stop' sequences by translating to Redwood token-level stop matcher and ensuring early termination sends a final finish_reason consistent with OpenAI semantics

Function/tool calling: map OpenAI function definitions to Redwood tool descriptors at registration time. During streaming, emit an interim event 'function_call' with partial 'arguments' until closed by model or runtime

Streaming: support both chunked SSE (text/event-stream) and HTTP/2 gRPC-like streaming. Provide a single abstraction layer that renders deltas into the appropriate wire format while maintaining chunk sequence numbers for diagnostics
Idempotency: respect an optional 'idempotency_key' header; if present and prior result exists, return cached response with a cache-control header and 'cached': true in metadata
progress_updates: 2025-02-19: Spike completed to validate SSE ordering with internal batching. Found 3ms median reordering under heavy batching (note in design doc)
2025-02-24: RFC posted to docs.redwood.internal; requested feedback from Console and Runtime teams (links above)

2025-02-27: Prototype PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1427. Prototype converts messages -> tokenized prompt and emits OpenAI-like chunked deltas. Initial perf regression: +6ms p50 end-to-end for small messages

2025-03-01: Design review (shared notes): prefer conservative mapping for function_call names to avoid accidental tool routing. Action: add explicit allowlist on project registration. Assigned: Security review for functions registration flow

2025-03-03: Integration test harness added for streaming conformance: tests/compat/streaming_spec.go added. Test patterns include partial-function-argument emission, stop-sequence mid-chunk, and rebuffer window sizing
2025-03-05: PR #1427 updated with sequence-window and argument-normalizer. Requested review from @mira, @samir. Next: add telemetry tags for 'compat-mode' and 'sequence_window_ms'
review_feedback: Mira Patel (Runtime): avoid adding long-tail timers in the hot path. Suggest moving reordering buffer into a non-blocking emission queue
Samir Gupta (Security): function registration must verify tool manifest signatures. Add a lightweight manifest schema check before exposing tool to compat shim
Hannah Lee (SDK): expose a client flag in SDKs to opt into 'openai_compat' per-request to avoid global tenant-wide toggles
test_plan: Unit: argument-normalizer tests covering nested JSON, trailing commas, and non-string values
Integration: end-to-end mapping test against a mock OpenAI client verifying SSE framing and final choices shape
Load: 10k concurrent short-chat sessions to validate sequence-window default sizing does not increase p50 by >10ms
Canary: enable compat shim for 1% of traffic on staging, collect 'compat-mode' telemetry and error rates over 48h
next_steps: Finish PR feedback loop and merge runtime changes (owner: Daniel)
Wire up manifest signature check endpoint and update function registration flow (owner: Security)
Add SDK opt-in flag and update docs/guides with migration notes (owner: SDK/Docs)
Schedule canary rollout and observe streaming error and latency metrics for 72h
notes: We intentionally do not emulate undocumented OpenAI quirks (edge tokenization differences) unless a customer shows a regression. Keep mapping deterministic and explicit
Telemetry: emit 'compat:openai_cc' tag and per-session 'sequence_window_ms' and 'function_call_count' counters
Consider a follow-up task to add a compatibility testbed that replays historical client traces to validate behavior across runtime changes
